title: Gluing the étale models of a torsor
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $G_0$ a sheaf of groups on $X_{\Et}$ and $T$ a
$\nu_X^*G_0$-torsor on $X_{\Proet}$. Then there is a $G_0$-torsor $T_0$ on $X_{\Et}$
and an isomorphism of torsors $\nu_X^*T_0\cong T$, unique up to unique
isomorphism. In particular $T$ is classical and has a trivializing étale
covering.

proof.text:
First fix the restriction identifications used throughout. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open], for any etale morphism $W	o X$ (in particular any open subscheme) the slice $X_{\Et}/W$ is $W_{\Et}$ as a site, not just at the level of abelian sheaves. Part (1) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies $X_{\Proet}/W$ with $W_{\Proet}$ and their set sheaves. The inclusion in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] views every etale object as weakly etale, so both site-identification hypotheses hold. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-slice-site-localization] to the continuous inclusion defining $
u_X$ in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. On the localized sites the inclusion is exactly the inclusion defining $
u_W$. Hence there is a natural isomorphism $r_{W,F}:(
u_X^*F)|_W\xrightarrow{\sim}
u_W^*(F|_W)$. Use these canonical identifications on all overlaps. For composable etale maps $Z	o W	o X$, denote this isomorphism by $r^X_{W,F}$. Under the sectionwise relocalization identifications, $r^X_{Z,F}=r^W_{Z,F|_W}\circ(r^X_{W,F})|_Z$. Indeed, the inclusion and forgetful slice functors commute on objects and arrows; the two comparison maps are adjunction mates of that same commuting composite square, so the adjunction bijection makes them equal. The isomorphisms preserve finite products since both routes are finite-limit-preserving inverse images; thus they identify the restricted group actions. Restricting a torsor gives a torsor: simple transitivity and a local section can be checked on the same objects and covering families of these slice sites.

source.place: Tag 03CF, lemma-localize-morphism; slice-site identifications as in the cited nodes

proof.text:
Choose a set-indexed affine open cover $X= igcup_aX_a$ (no quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness is required). An open cover is a cover in both sites by [sk-def-pe-site] and [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. By step 1 the restriction of $T$ is a $
u_{X_a}^*(G_0|_{X_a})$-torsor. Apply [det-pe-torsor-comparison-affine] to each affine scheme $X_a$: obtain a $G_0|_{X_a}$-torsor $T_{0,a}$, an equivariant isomorphism $\alpha_a:
u_{X_a}^*T_{0,a}\xrightarrow{\sim}T|_{X_a}$, and an affine etale surjection $W_a	o X_a$ with $T_{0,a}(W_a)
e\varnothing$. The same argument includes $X=\varnothing$, using an empty affine cover.

source.place: Tag 099X, lemma-compare-cohomology-nonabelian, reduction to an affine base; blueprint proof paragraph 1

proof.text:
Put $X_{ab}=X_a\cap X_b$. Under step 1 the map $ eta_{ab}=\alpha_b^{-1}\circ\alpha_a$ is an isomorphism from $
u_{X_{ab}}^*(T_{0,a}|_{X_{ab}})$ to $
u_{X_{ab}}^*(T_{0,b}|_{X_{ab}})$. Full faithfulness in [det-pe-classical-sheaves-unit], applied to the scheme $X_{ab}$, gives a unique sheaf map $\phi_{ab}$ with $
u^*\phi_{ab}= eta_{ab}$. Lift $ eta_{ab}^{-1}$ as well; faithfulness applied to their two composites proves that $\phi_{ab}$ is invertible. Write $m_a,m_b$ for the restricted actions. Since $ eta_{ab}$ is equivariant, the pullbacks of $\phi_{ab}\circ m_a$ and $m_b\circ(\mathrm{id}_{G_0}	imes\phi_{ab})$ agree. The finite-product preservation in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] identifies their domains, and faithfulness makes the two maps equal. Thus $\phi_{ab}$ is equivariant. On $X_{abc}$, cancellation gives $ eta_{bc} eta_{ab}=\alpha_c^{-1}\alpha_a= eta_{ac}$; faithfulness on this scheme gives $\phi_{bc}\phi_{ab}=\phi_{ac}$. Likewise $\phi_{aa}=\mathrm{id}$. None of these overlaps is assumed affine.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, descent and identities of the transition maps; full faithfulness is Stacks Tag 099T

proof.text: Apply [lem-pe-site-sheaf-gluing] to the covering $\{X_a\to X\}$ of $X_{\Et}$ and the sheaves $T_{0,a}$ with the isomorphisms $\phi_{ab}$ from step 3. The small sites and the set-indexed cover fit the universe convention in that lemma. Since $X$ is final in its small etale site, the slice over $X$ is the original site. Using the site identifications fixed in step 1, the lemma gives a sheaf of sets $T_0$ on $X_{\Et}$ and isomorphisms $e_a:T_0|_{X_a}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{0,a}$ satisfying $\phi_{ab}e_a=e_b$ on every overlap.

Define the action on $T_0$ explicitly. For an etale $V\to X$, $g\in G_0(V)$ and $t\in T_0(V)$, set $V_a=V\times_XX_a$. The sections $e_a^{-1}(g|_{V_a}\cdot e_a(t|_{V_a}))$ agree on $V_a\times_VV_b$, by the equivariance of $\phi_{ab}$ and $\phi_{ab}e_a=e_b$. The sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] gives a unique section $g\cdot t$ on $V$. Restriction, the identity law and associativity hold because they hold on every $V_a$ and the same uniqueness applies. For $t,t'\in T_0(V)$, the local torsor structures give a unique $g_a\in G_0(V_a)$ sending $t|_{V_a}$ to $t'|_{V_a}$. Freeness makes these agree on overlaps; the sheaf axiom for $G_0$ glues them to a unique $g\in G_0(V)$. Finally the chosen sections over the etale surjections $W_a\to X_a$ of step 2 give local sections of $T_0$ on a jointly surjective etale family over $X$, and on every test object after base change. These are precisely simple transitivity and local nonemptiness in [def-constructible-torsor], so $T_0$ is a $G_0$-torsor.

source.place: Tag 04TR, componentwise structures; elementary sheaf-axiom argument, with the map-gluing formula of Tag 04TQ

proof.text:
The local maps $A_a=\alpha_a\circ
u_{X_a}^*(e_a)\circ r_{X_a,T_0}$ are equivariant isomorphisms $(
u_X^*T_0)|_{X_a}	o T|_{X_a}$. On $X_{ab}$ the equations $
u^*\phi_{ab}=\alpha_b^{-1}\alpha_a$ and $\phi_{ab}e_a=e_b$ give $A_b=A_a$; naturality of $r$ from step 1 makes these equations equations between the actual restricted maps. For a pro-etale object $V	o X$ and $s\in(
u_X^*T_0)(V)$, apply $A_a$ to $s|_{V	imes_XX_a}$ and glue the resulting compatible sections of $T$ over the open cover of $V$. The sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] makes this a unique section $\alpha_V(s)$, natural in $V$. For a morphism $h:V^{\prime}	o V$, both $h^*\alpha_V(s)$ and $\alpha_{V^{\prime}}(h^*s)$ restrict over $V^{\prime}	imes_XX_a$ to $A_a(h^*s)$ by naturality of $A_a$; uniqueness of gluing proves naturality of $\alpha$. Define $B_V(t)$ for $t\in T(V)$ to be the unique section of $(
u_X^*T_0)(V)$ whose restriction over $V	imes_XX_a$ is $A_a^{-1}(t|_{V	imes_XX_a})$. These local sections agree because $A_a=A_b$ on overlaps. Restriction of $B_V(t)$ along $h$ and $B_{V^{\prime}}(h^*t)$ have equal local restrictions, so $B$ is a sheaf map. The restrictions of $B\alpha$ and $\alpha B$ are $A_a^{-1}A_a$ and $A_aA_a^{-1}$ respectively; the sheaf axiom makes both composites identities. For local sections $g,s$, the sections $\alpha(gs)$ and $g\alpha(s)$ restrict to $A_a(gs)=gA_a(s)$, so they are equal by uniqueness of gluing. Thus $\alpha:
u_X^*T_0\xrightarrow{\sim}T$ is an isomorphism of torsors. This uses the fact in [sk-def-pe-site] that every open cover is a pro-etale cover, with no finiteness requirement on the affine cover of $X$.

source.place: Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps, explicit application of its sectionwise formula; blueprint proof paragraph 2

proof.text: Uniqueness concerns the pair $(T_0,\alpha)$. If $(T'_0,\alpha')$ is another such pair, full faithfulness in [det-pe-classical-sheaves-unit] on $X$ gives a unique $f:T_0\to T'_0$ with $\nu_X^*f=(\alpha')^{-1}\alpha$. Its inverse is the unique lift of $\alpha^{-1}\alpha'$, as verified by faithfulness. The equivariance equation for $f$ follows by applying faithfulness to the two maps out of $G_0\times T_0$; their pullbacks are equal because $(\alpha')^{-1}\alpha$ is equivariant and [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] preserves finite products. Hence $f$ is the unique torsor isomorphism satisfying $\alpha'\circ\nu_X^*f=\alpha$. This is the asserted uniqueness up to unique isomorphism, with the specified comparison to $T$ included.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, uniqueness; explicit fully faithful lift on torsor maps

proof.text: By [det-pe-classical-sheaves-image], the isomorphism $T\cong\nu_X^*T_0$ makes $T$ classical. The composites $W_a\to X_a\to X$ from step 2 are etale and jointly surjective, so they form an etale covering by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. A chosen section of $T_{0,a}(W_a)$ trivializes $T_0$ there: $g\mapsto g\cdot s_a$ is an isomorphism by simple transitivity, also on every further test object. Pulling this isomorphism back and using step 1 and $\alpha$ from step 6 trivializes $T$ on $W_a$. Thus the asserted etale trivializing covering is an actual covering of $X$, not just a collection of local covers.
